decision: Retire the optional WebGL document bridge; retain the normal Skia/WebGL compositor and CPU upload fallback.
scope: These are same-AOT-artifact persistent-versus-WebGL document-bridge comparisons on the same runner within each workload. Independent jobs and source snapshots are not pooled.
Chromium with SwiftShader measures software graphics, not physical GPU throughput or physical presentation.
Pan medians did not improve. Zoom gains were small and varied between source snapshots; favorable d0 trials are retained.
Reduced renderer-thread CPU did not establish a consistent end-to-end interaction improvement.
The DPR1 timing fixture gates passed. Later Welcome lifecycle coverage passed, while extended SVG coverage was incomplete with independently reproduced failures on a44 and 523.
The d0 extended SVG job was still running at this evidence checkpoint. Earlier failures must not be claimed as completed d0 validation.
This decision concerns canvasBridge=webgl, not renderer=skia or Uno's normal WebGL fallback.

metric_definitions.elapsed_ms: Wall-clock workload window, including 120 offered trusted inputs and observed application callback completion.
metric_definitions.renderer_thread_cpu_ms: CDP ThreadTime active renderer main-thread CPU; excludes GPU and worker CPU.
metric_definitions.task_elapsed_ms: CDP TaskDuration elapsed task time; may include blocking and is not active CPU.
metric_definitions.offered_operations_per_second: 120 divided by measured workload wall time; not displayed frames per second.
metric_definitions.callbacks_and_submissions: Observed completed application callbacks and visible WebGPU canvas submissions; not presentation events or proven input-to-new-pixels causality.
metric_definitions.post_window: Capture/restore durations are outside primary timing and include automation/image analysis. Older a44/523 reports did not collect them; null means unavailable. This bridge exposes no matched GPU queue-drain measurement.
